en.name: Mung beans, dry (vacuum-sealed)
en.summary: Vacuum-sealed dry mung beans keep about 8–10 years in the cupboard — an order of magnitude longer than the same beans in an ordinary bag. The vacuum, not the bean, is what does it, so the figure holds only while the seal is intact.
en.pantry: About 8–10 years in a cool, dark, dry place, for an unopened vacuum pack. What buys that span is the removal of oxygen, which stops the seed oil oxidising, together with a barrier that insects and moisture cannot cross. It is a long-term storage figure rather than an everyday one, so it comes with conditions: the pack must be intact, stored cool and out of the light, and any pack that has lost its vacuum and gone soft or puffy has reverted to being an ordinary bag of beans. Once you open it, the same short rules apply as to any bagged dry bean — decant into an airtight jar, keep it dry, and use it within a much more ordinary span.
en.fridge: No refrigerator figure is given for vacuum-sealed mung beans, and none is needed: a sealed pack in a cupboard already outlasts almost anything else in a kitchen. Cold is only worth considering for beans you have opened, in a hot, humid climate, and then the figures for ordinary bagged beans are the ones that apply. Let any container come back to room temperature before opening it so condensation does not settle on the beans.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given, and there is nothing to gain. A vacuum pack is already about as stable as a dry food gets, and freezer space is worth more to something perishable. Note too that a very long stored life does not mean a very long cooking life: beans harden as they age, so a pack opened after many years will need a long soak and a long simmer, and may stay firm however patient you are.
spoilage: A pack that has lost its vacuum, gone soft or puffed up.
A musty or mouldy smell when the pack is opened.
Beans with small bored holes, or dust and webbing inside a compromised pack.
Beans that will not soften after long soaking and simmering — age, not spoilage.
tips: Check the vacuum before storing a pack for the long term; a soft pack is not sealed.
Store the packs cool, dark and off a concrete floor.
Once opened, treat it exactly like an ordinary bag of dry beans.
Plan for longer cooking with beans that have been stored for years.

faq.q: How long do vacuum-sealed mung beans keep?
faq.a: About 8–10 years in a cool, dark, dry place while the pack is unopened and the vacuum intact.

faq.q: Do they still keep that long once opened?
faq.a: No. Once the seal is broken they are ordinary dry beans again — decant into an airtight jar and keep them dry.

faq.q: Will beans stored for years still cook properly?
faq.a: They are safe, but they harden with age. Expect a long soak and a long simmer, and some may never soften fully.

zh.name: 綠豆（真空包乾豆）
zh.summary: 真空包裝的乾綠豆在櫥櫃裡大約可放 8～10 年，比同樣的豆子裝在一般袋子裡長了一個數量級。做到這件事的是真空而不是豆子本身，所以這個數字只在封口完好時成立。
zh.pantry: 未開封的真空包，放在陰涼、避光、乾燥處約 8～10 年。撐起這段時間的是「抽掉氧氣」——種子油脂不再氧化——加上一層蟲和水氣都穿不過的阻隔。這是長期儲備用的數字而不是日常數字，所以附帶條件：包裝必須完整、存放陰涼避光；任何真空跑掉、變軟或鼓起的包裝，就等於退回成一包普通的豆子。一旦開封，規則就和所有袋裝乾豆一樣——倒進密封罐、保持乾燥，並在普通得多的期限內用完。
zh.fridge: 真空包綠豆沒有給冷藏數字，也不需要：一包密封的豆子放在櫥櫃裡，已經比廚房裡幾乎所有東西都耐放。只有開封後、又住在濕熱地區時才值得考慮冷藏，而那時適用的是一般袋裝乾豆的數字。任何容器開封前都先回到室溫，免得水氣凝在豆子上。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給冷凍期限，也沒有任何好處。真空包本來就已經是乾貨能達到的穩定極限，冷凍庫的空間留給容易壞的東西比較划算。另外要提醒：能放很久不代表能煮得好。豆子會隨年紀變硬，放了很多年才開的一包，要泡很久、煮很久，甚至再有耐心也不一定會軟。
spoilage: 包裝真空跑掉、變軟或鼓起。
豆子上有蛀孔，或破損包裝內有粉屑和絲網。
泡很久煮很久還是不軟——那是年紀，不是腐敗。
tips: 長期存放前先確認真空狀態；摸起來鬆軟就代表沒封好。
包裝放陰涼避光處，不要直接貼著水泥地面。
一旦開封，就完全比照普通袋裝乾豆處理。
放了好幾年的豆子，要預留更長的烹煮時間。

faq.q: 真空包的乾綠豆可以放多久？
faq.a: 未開封、真空完好，放陰涼避光乾燥處約 8～10 年。

faq.q: 開封後還能放那麼久嗎？
faq.a: 不行。封口一破它就是普通乾豆了——請倒進密封罐並保持乾燥。

faq.q: 放了好幾年的豆子還煮得軟嗎？
faq.a: 吃是安全的，但它會隨年紀變硬。請預期要泡很久、煮很久，有些甚至不會完全煮軟。
